_comment: Tolerance file of the CUDA<->Luisa parity harness (S0 / T9.3a).
Rules (03-parity-harness.md §5.2): every non-default number carries a _why entry
keyed by its dotted path; 'iterations'/'counts' are compared exactly, never with a
band; a tolerance may only be loosened together with a note in
The defaults are all 0.0 on purpose: bit-exactness is the strongest gate there is,
and NO tolerance value in this file has been validated against a real CUDA
reference yet (the CUDA backend cannot be built in this environment -- see
AGENT_ENV_BRIEF.md:13). The first cross-backend run must either stay exact or add
an override with a measured number and its _why.

_why.defaults.abs: Bit-exact: Class A. Two runs of the same backend on the same machine must not differ by a single ulp; a bigger number here would hide a real ordering change.
_why.defaults.eps_scale: The relative denominator is max(|ref|, eps_scale). 1.0 keeps a near-zero reference from turning an absolute epsilon into an unbounded relative error.
_why.defaults.scalars.float_abs: Scalar floats are compared exactly by default; last_line_search_alpha / last_ccd_toi / last_cfl_alpha are deterministic for a fixed scene.
_why.defaults.scalars.ignore[0]: counters.sync_ms is wall-clock time measured by the backend (src/backends/luisa/sim_engine.cpp frame stats). It is the only non-deterministic field of the scalars probe: it must never gate a parity result, and the iteration/flag fields next to it are what the structural gate uses.
_why.defaults.scalars.ignore[1]: Same as counters.sync_ms; recorded so an alternative spelling of the timing counter is ignored too instead of failing the first run that reports it.
